PE1-17.hint: On the unit circle \(\cos\theta = x\), \(\sin\theta = y\), and \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{y}{x}\). For (a), find the reference angle and the quadrant, then decide the sign.
slips: Giving \(+\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\). In Quadrant IV the \(y\)-coordinate is negative.
Giving \(\tan\theta = y\) because the point is on the unit circle. That is true for sine, not tangent.

PE1-18.hint: Sine is the \(y\)-coordinate and cosine is the \(x\)-coordinate. Tangent is \(\dfrac{y}{x}\), so it is positive when \(x\) and \(y\) have the same sign. The reference angle is the acute angle between the terminal side and the \(x\)-axis.
slips: Using only one condition. Two quadrants satisfy \(\sin\theta < 0\); the tangent condition picks between them.
Giving \(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\) itself as the reference angle. The reference angle is acute; in Quadrant II, subtract \(\theta\) from \(\pi\).
Swapping which coordinate is sine and which is cosine.
PE1-18.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

parts.a: \(-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\). The reference angle is \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\), and in Quadrant IV sine is negative.

parts.q: The terminal point \(P(x,y) = \left(\dfrac{5}{13}, -\dfrac{12}{13}\right)\) lies on the unit circle at angle \(\theta\). Find \(\tan\theta\).
In which quadrant must the terminal side of \(\theta\) lie if \(\sin\theta \lt  0\) and \(\tan\theta \gt  0\)?
parts.a: Quadrant III. \(\sin\theta \lt  0\) means Quadrant III or IV, and \(\tan\theta \gt  0\) means Quadrant I or III. Only III satisfies both.

parts.q: On the unit circle, the angle \(\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\) has terminal point \(P\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\). Find the reference angle, then \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos\theta\).
